title: Rate-controller state divergence causing tenant lockouts across Hosted/Dedicated/Private
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Summary: Several customers reported sudden opaque 429s and sustained throughput loss across Hosted, Dedicated and Private deployments. Alerts and PagerDuty incidents began 2026-02-28 03:12 UTC. Impacted tenants experienced near-total request rejection for minutes->hours despite capacity being available. This ticket centralizes the escalation, triage, mitigation, and long-term fixes for a state divergence in the rate/quota controller and quota ledger reconciliation logic.

Observed symptoms: tenants hit immediate 429s without corresponding spikes in incoming traffic; token counters showed negative or stale values in the reconciliation dashboard; Dedicated and Private control-plane logs show lease renewals failing while Hosted control plane continued to accept requests; customers reported partial recovery after service restarts.

Scope: multiple Hosted customers (3 high-volume production accounts), 2 Dedicated clusters, and 4 Private installations (customer-managed) running older runtime revisions. All reported the same user-facing symptom but root-causes vary by environment: Hosted: controller rollout + replica bias; Dedicated: autoscaler interplay; Private: config schema mismatch during edge upgrade.

Why this is critical: customer-facing outages, escalations to CSM/Support, potential SLA breaches for Dedicated customers, and loss of trust for Private customers performing air-gapped upgrades.
timeline:
2026-02-28 03:12 UTC: PagerDuty triggered by high 429 rate for tenant X.
2026-02-28 03:18 UTC: First customer escalation — CSM opened a support ticket.
2026-02-28 03:25 UTC: On-call identified anomalous ledger entries (lease expiry timestamps far in the past) in reconciliation service.
2026-02-28 03:40 UTC: Emergency bridge with infra/runtime/owners; initial mitigation - whitelist affected tenants to bypass strict exhaustion check.
2026-02-28 04:15 UTC: Hotfix deployed to Hosted (patch to TTL calculation & retry for lease renewals). Immediate reduction in 429s for Hosted customers.
2026-02-28 06:00 UTC: Investigated Dedicated clusters — found autoscaler backpressure combining with new controller semantics causing token double-consumption. Temporary workaround applied to relax autoscaler threshold.
2026-03-01 09:30 UTC: Private customers were guided to apply a small config patch to align quota schema; two customers applied and reported recovery.
2026-03-02 14:00 UTC: Root cause confirmed (see root_cause). Planning next release and reconciliation migration job.
mitigations:
1) Hotfix deployed to Hosted runtime that normalizes lease TTL units and adds robust renewal retry with exponential backoff.
2) Tenant whitelist and emergency bypass lane for P0 customers to avoid strict exhaustion checks while we reconcile state.
3) Temporary autoscaler threshold relaxation on affected Dedicated clusters to avoid combined backpressure.
4) Private customer support playbook: small schema/config patch and step-by-step upgrade notes.
5) Increased alerting granularity: per-tenant reconciliation deltas and alert thresholds for >10% stale counters.
6) Customer comms: incident postmortem draft and targeted notifications to impacted accounts.
root_cause: A multi-factor failure: during a refactor of the quota ledger reconciliation path we introduced a unit mismatch and a semantic change in lease handling. One code path used milliseconds while the reconciler assumed seconds, causing leases to appear expired and triggering aggressive exhaustion marks. Additionally, a concurrent change to the autoscaler/backpressure logic caused double-consumption of burst tokens under specific load patterns. For Private deployments, older config schemas did not include the new lease-grace field, so the reconciler treated those tenants as permanently exhausted until a restart or manual patch. Cross-region replication lag amplified the problem for Dedicated customers when leader elections coincided with TTL expiries, producing transient but repeated lockouts.
resolution:
Short-term: hotfix released to Hosted; workarounds for Dedicated and Private documented and applied.
Medium-term (next release): patch runtime to unify TTL units across code paths, add idempotent lease-renewal, and harden autoscaler interaction tests.
Long-term: introduce a ledger-reconciliation migration job that scans and repairs drifted counters, add e2e tests that simulate replication lag and leader elections, and ship per-tenant diff alerts to catch divergence before customer impact.
Follow-ups (tracked in sub-issues): automated migration tool, add reconciliation runbook, expand canary criteria for controller rollouts (include lease-renewal smoke), and a retrospective with product/CS for customer-facing improvements.
